content.title: About
content.content: Pound cake is a classic English dessert consisting of a dense, moist sponge that is soaked with syrup and covered with a glaze. It traditionally weighs about 450 g (one pound) and is often served with fruit, nuts, or buttercream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pound cake originated in the 19th century in England as a simple way to use leftover birthday cake.
The name comes from the cake’s weight – one pound (≈ 450 g).
The original recipe used only eggs, sugar, flour and butter, without any leavening agents.
It is commonly decorated with dried fruits, nuts and lemon zest, giving it a distinctive aroma.
In the United States a similar dessert is called “pound cake,” although the texture may differ.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The cake provides carbohydrates and fats that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Calcium from dairy
items.content: Butter and milk in the recipe deliver calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and flour are rich in B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from fruit
items.content: When served with berries or dried fruit, the cake gains antioxidants that protect cells.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Pound cake contains a considerable amount of sugar, which can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, the cake is calorie‑rich; moderate consumption is advised for weight‑watching individuals.

items.title: Egg and dairy allergies
items.content: People allergic to eggs, milk or gluten should avoid this cake.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter may introduce trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pound cake in slice‑sized pieces, often with a cup of tea or coffee. It can be enjoyed on its own or paired with berry sauce, whipped cream, ice cream, or fresh fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate for up to 5 days. Bring the cake to room temperature before serving to retain its soft texture.
